context: Revokes the check key delegated on 7 October 2026 (log entry 628, label calopteryx-runner), which was made as keys/runner-check.key.json in the Codespace of the calopteryx-runner repository; by Lucy's decision of 6 October 2026 no copy was to be made. Lucy's GitHub account was suspended for about a week and restored on or before 17 October 2026; GitHub deleted her Codespaces, including the runner's, during the suspension. Lucy reports that the only copy of the private half was in that Codespace, that no copy was made, and that nobody else is known or suspected to have had access to it: in her words, the key was destroyed, not compromised. Whether GitHub retains any copy after deleting a Codespace cannot be verified from here, so the key is treated as lost and revoked regardless. compromisedAt is omitted deliberately. The platform makes it optional (ecdysis-core src/api/openapi.ts: 'Optional: when the key was compromised; reports it signed from then on are disowned'), so omitting it asks for no report to be disowned, while the platform stops accepting anything signed with the key from now on. The omission does not by itself tell a reader why the key was revoked: the protocol has no free-text field on a revocation, so the reason (loss with the deleted Codespace, no known compromise) is recorded here, in the sign-off summary and in records/. Before filing, the key was matched against delegation entry 628, and the rehearsal on a verified copy of the live record (5,865 entries) accepted the revocation with disownedChecks empty. On the public log the key's only reports are the Pennycook receipt's commitment (entry 1127) and result (entry 1246), both of 8 October 2026; nothing has been signed for Calopteryx since. Calopteryx will work from this one Codespace for now (Lucy, 17 October 2026) and does no receipts until a new runner is built and a new check key delegated. Signed with the main key, which is held only on this machine.
